vectors.desc: nil selector 0: the one nil state, absent
deriv: envelope (c4 DD closure): header + root DESC + value - root DESC E0 D8 08 INTERFACE, the minimal empty-body descriptor; nil roots are enveloped, the nil token rides after the DESC (WF-22 :623, :702-706)

the nil sort is derived from the static type of the position, never read from the token (WF-15); NIL-class token 00: selector 0 = absent - the one nil state, no selector encodes a nil sort (WF-15; WF-23)

vectors.desc: nil selector 4: zero-size marker — non-nil pointer to a zero-size target
deriv: envelope (c4 DD closure): header + root DESC + value - root DESC E0 D7 POINTER, type-ref DESC TUPLE(0) E0 D2 00 - a zero-size target, distinct carrier from V-51's empty-struct target (WF-22 :612, :617, :683-685)

NIL token 04: selector 4 = the zero-size marker of section 7.1 - a non-nil pointer to a zero-size target, no REF and no address; the marker and nil selector 0 stay byte-distinct (WF-15; WF-24 :789-790, :826-827)
envelope (c4 DD closure): would-be canonical prefix - root DESC E0 D8 08 INTERFACE rides, the stream halts at the first offending byte (WF-22 :623, :702-706)
NIL token 07: selector 7 is neither 0 nor 4 - reserved band, a decoder rejects it (WF-15); class nil_reserved_selector

vectors.desc: nil slice vs empty slice: nil token vs VIEW len 0 over a zero-length blob backing
deriv: root DESC SLICE kind 3 = E0 D3, one elem type-ref DESC BLOB E0 D8 0E (WF-22)
value 1: NIL token 00 - a nil slice is the nil token of WF-15, not a view (WF-17; WF-15)
value 2: backing BLOB L=0 E=0 = token 70 00 (WF-14), interns id 2 after DESC ids 0,1 (WF-24); view form 0: off=0, len=extent=L=0, id-only body 90 02 (WF-17)
nil is never confused with empty: the VIEW len 0 is a non-nil empty slice (WF-15)

vectors.desc: nil map vs empty map: nil token vs MAP count 0
deriv: root DESC MAP kind 5 = E0 D5, two type-refs: key DESC STRING, elem DESC BOOL (WF-22)
value 1: NIL token 00 - a nil map is the nil token of WF-15 and never interns (WF-18; WF-15)
value 2: token A0 = class A, fused inline pair count 0 - an empty non-nil map is a record like any other; nil is never confused with empty (WF-18; WF-15)

vectors.desc: typed nil via descriptor: pointer position carries the dynamic type's DESC then the nil body
deriv: root DESC INTERFACE = E0 D8 08, empty body - the reference position's static grain (WF-22)
typed nil in an interface position: the pointer position carries the dynamic type's DESC - INT width 4 inline 04 - then the nil body 00 (WF-24; WF-22)
the descriptor that is present resolves the chain at its top level; the nil sort is derived, never read from the token (WF-15)

vectors.desc: ZST marker in a typed pointer position: non-nil pointer to the empty struct
deriv: root DESC POINTER kind 7 = E0 D7, one type-ref: DESC STRUCT kind 0 = E0 D0, body ARG n=0 inline 00 - the empty struct, a zero-size target (WF-22)
value: NIL token 04 - the zero-size marker in a typed pointer position: a non-nil pointer to the empty struct, no REF and no address (WF-15; WF-24)
reference identity of zero-size targets is neither preserved nor observable; the marker and nil selector 0 stay byte-distinct (WF-24)
